title: Analysis of mouse intestinal organoid culture with conditioned media isolated from mucosal enteric glial cells
protocol: Euthanize mice using an authorized, legal method.
Sterilize the abdomen with 70% Ethanol.
Make an incision into the abdominal cavity from the external genitalia to the rib cage by cutting abdominal musculature on both sides.
Lift the liver and cut the intestine from the stomach at the pyloric sphincter.
Cut across the large intestine just prior to the anus to release the whole gut.
Cut the mesenteric attachment of the intestine if necessary and gently pull the gut out of the abdominal cavity.
Place the gut in a petri dish filled with ice-cold gut buffer.
Tear the mesentery to unfold the gut.
Separate the small intestine from the colon by cutting at the ileocecal junction.
Flush the intestine of fecal content with ice-cold gut buffer using a 1 mL syringe mounted with a 1,000 μL tip.
Use forceps gently to push out any remaining feces if necessary.
Cut the intestine into three equal pieces roughly corresponding to duodenum, jejunum, and ileum.
Cut open each segment longitudinally so that the inside of the intestine is facing up.
Gently scrape out the villi using a slide.
Discard the part of the intestinal lumen remaining on the slide.
Place the intestinal segments in a conical 50 mL tube filled with 20 mL gut buffer.
Invert the tube gently three times.
Discard the supernatant.
Recover intestinal segments with forceps.
Cut the segments into 0.5 cm pieces.
Transfer the pieces to a 15 mL tube containing 10 mL of ice-cold chelating buffer.
Shake the tube using an orbital shaker or rocking plate at 4°C for 25 minutes at 20 rpm.
Gently invert the tube and filter the solution through a 100 μm strainer into a 50 mL conical tube.
Transfer the intestine pieces into a 50 mL conical tube containing 25 mL ice-cold crypt dissociation buffer.
Orient the tube at 45° to the ground and shake it for 4–6 minutes with gentle and regular motion.
Every 2 minutes, place the tube on ice to rest for 30 seconds.
Pipette 50 μL of the solution and check under the microscope for crypt enrichment.
If necessary, shake the tube for an additional 2 minutes, and check again.
Place the tube on ice.
Allow fragments to settle down.
Filter the solution through a 70 μm filter into a 50 mL conical tube on ice.
Add 10 mL of crypt dissociation buffer to wash the strainer.
Discard the strainer.
Centrifuge the crypt-containing solution at 150 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Carefully discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of ice-cold PBS 1×.
Count the number of crypts in 10 μL.
Determine the total number of crypts by multiplying the counted crypts by 1,000.
Transfer the volume required for 300 crypts/well to a new 15 mL conical tube.
On ice, mix Matrigel with ENR media at a 70:30 ratio.
Use 50 μL of this 70% Matrigel per well.
Pipette the mixture slowly to avoid introducing bubbles.
Gently resuspend crypt pellets in the required volume of 70% Matrigel until clumps become fully dissociated.
Incubate the plate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 15 min to allow Matrigel polymerization.
Add 350 μL of pre-warmed ENR media per well.
Culture the organoids at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Replace the media with fresh pre-warmed ENR media every 4 days.
Euthanize mice using an authorized, legal method approved by the institution where the research is conducted.
Sterilize the abdomen with 70% Ethanol.
Make an incision into the abdominal cavity from the external genitalia to the rib cage by cutting abdominal musculature on both sides.
Lift the liver and cut the intestine from the stomach at the pyloric sphincter.
Cut across the large intestine just prior to the anus to release the whole gut.
Cut the mesenteric attachment of the intestine if necessary and gently pull the gut out of the abdominal cavity.
Place the gut in a petri dish filled with ice-cold gut buffer.
Tear the mesentery to unfold the gut.
Remove any residual mesentery from the tissue.
Cut the gut at the ileocecal junction to separate the small intestine from the colon.
Flush fecal content from the intestine with ice-cold gut buffer using a 1 mL syringe mounted with a 1,000 μL tip.
Cut the intestine into three pieces: duodenum, jejunum, and ileum.
Remove the longitudinal muscle from each intestinal segment.
Separate the wooden part of a cotton swab from its cotton tip.
Soak the wooden part of the cotton swab in cold gut buffer.
Thread one intestinal segment onto the pre-wetted wooden stick.
Make vertical incisions along the intestine using a scalpel or razor blade.
Apply gentle horizontal strokes with the pre-wetted cotton swab to tease away the longitudinal muscle.
Continue this motion until the longitudinal muscle peels away from the intestine.
Discard the removed longitudinal muscle.
Cut open the intestinal segment using forceps/razor blade.
Transfer the intestinal tissue to a 50 mL conical tube filled with gut buffer on ice.
Cut the intestinal segments into 0.5 cm pieces.
Transfer the pieces to a 50 mL conical tube filled with 25 mL of ice-cold EGC isolation solution.
Gently shake the tube in an orbital shaker or rocking plate at 4°C for 15 minutes.
Triturate the tissue-solution mixture by pipetting up and down 20 times using a moistened 10 mL plastic pipette.
Filter the mixture through a 100 μm strainer, recovering the tissues with forceps.
Transfer recovered tissues to a new 50 mL conical tube filled with 25 mL of ice-cold EGC isolation solution.
Repeat filtration steps until the solution is clear.
Transfer tissue pieces to a 15 mL conical tube containing 10 mL of Corning Cell Recovery solution and rock for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Triturate the tissue-solution mixture by pipetting up and down 20 times using a moistened 5 mL plastic pipette.
Filter through a 40 μm strainer in a 50 mL conical tube.
Discard the tissue pieces.
Wash the strainer with 2 mL of cold PBS.
Transfer the flow-through to a 15 mL conical tube.
Spin at 2,000 g and 4°C for 5 min.
Gently resuspend pellets in 1 mL of EGC culture media.
Plate 330 μL of cell suspension in a well containing 170 μL of EGC culture media.
After 24 h, slowly pipette off the media containing non-adherent stromal cells.
Gently rinse with PBS.
Replace with fresh pre-warmed EGC culture media.
Cells can be used for experiments 3–4 days after plating.
Aspirate the EGC culture media after 3–4 days of culture.
Wash the wells twice with PBS 1×.
Add 500 μL of fresh pre-warmed EGC culture media without serum and GDNF.
Remove serum from the culture to avoid adding extra growth factors.
Collect serum-free EGC conditioned media into a 15 mL conical tube after 24 hours.
Pool all wells from one mouse together in the conical tube.
Filter the EGC-CM through a syringe with a 0.22 μm pore size filter.
Store filtered EGC-CM at -80°C for later use or thaw it at 37°C when needed.
Mix EGC-CM with ENR media at a 50:50 ratio (125 μL of EGC-CM + 125 μL ENR media per well).
Incubate the solution at 37°C for 10 minutes.
Aspirate ENR media from organoid culture after 4 days.
Add 350 μL of ENR:EGC-CM mix to the organoids.
Incubate the organoids at 37°C and analyze them 48 h–72 h later.
Decontaminate pipettors, benchtops, centrifuge, and ice bucket with RNAse Away® or equivalent surface decontamination solution.
Use RNAse-free tips, tubes, PBS 1×, and H2O throughout the procedure.
Remove media from organoid culture and add 400 μL of ice-cold PBS 1× per well.
Incubate the plate on ice for 5 min.
Break up the Matrigel-organoid dome by pipetting up and down.
Pool two wells into a 15 mL conical tube filled with 5 mL ice-cold PBS 1×.
Pipette up and down with a 1,000 μL pipette 15 times in the conical tube.
Centrifuge at 150 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the pellet in 350 μL of Qiagen RLT buffer supplemented with 1% β-mercaptoethanol.
Vortex the tubes for 30 s to fully lyse the organoids.
Spin the tubes at 150 g for 1 min at 4°C.
Transfer the lysate to a RNAse-free 1.5 mL tube.
Snap freeze the lysate in dry ice and store at -80°C until RNA extraction is needed.
Proceed with the Qiagen RNeasy Plus Mini extraction kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Measure RNA yield and concentration with a Nanodrop spectrophotometer.
Use ≤ 50 ng of RNA for one qPCR well.
Perform reverse transcription according to manufacturers’ guidelines.
Pause point: Store cDNA at −80°C until ready to load qPCR plate.
Run qPCR following manufacturers’ instructions.
For 1 qPCR well: Mix 5 μL of SYBR green master mix with 4 μL cDNA and 1 μL primer mix (forward + reverse at 10 μM).
Load qPCR plate on ice.
Analyze data using the 2-ΔΔCT method.
Pre-warm 5 mL of TrypLE 1× at 37°C.
Remove media from organoid culture and add 400 μL of ice-cold PBS per well.
Incubate the plate on ice for 5 min.
Break up the Matrigel-organoid dome by pipetting up and down.
Pool all the wells for one mouse/condition into a 15 mL conical tube filled with 3 mL of ice-cold PBS.
Pipette up and down 15 times to further dissociate the Matrigel.
Start with at least 6 wells of organoids for one data point.
Centrifuge the sample at 150 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of pre-warmed TrypLe 1×.
Incubate the suspension at 37°C for 3 minutes.
Dissociate organoids into single cells by passing them through a syringe with a 18G blunt needle 15 times.
Neutralize the TrypLe by adding 10 mL of cold gut buffer.
Centrifuge the sample at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 μL of gut buffer.
Add CD24-Pacific Blue antibody (1/500 dilution) to the sample.
Add EPCAM-APC antibody (1/500 dilution) to the sample.
Add propidium iodide (1/1000 dilution) as a live dye to exclude dead cells.
Incubate the samples for 20 minutes on ice in the dark or covered with an aluminum sheet.
Set aside 50 μL of control sample before adding antibodies.
Add 5 mL of gut buffer to wash off excess antibody.
Spin at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 μL of gut buffer.
Proceed to flow cytometry acquisition and analysis.
